Definition-based extraction

Definition-based extraction builds real FHIR resources — a Patient, a Condition, an Observation, and so on — by mapping a questionnaire's answers to the fields of those resources. This is the how-to; for the concept and how it compares to the other mechanisms, see Extraction.

How the mapping works

Two pieces drive it:

  1. Mark a group as producing a resource. A group annotated with the definition-extract extension becomes one resource instance. Its resource type comes from the definition on the group (or its children).
  2. Point each answer at a field. Give the child items an item.definition that names the target element — a URL of the form .../StructureDefinition/{Type}#{path}. The answer to that item is written to that field on the new resource.

Nested paths such as name.family are supported. The builder knows each element's type and whether it repeats, so a coded answer becomes the right kind of value (a codeable concept, a coding or a plain code), a single-valued element stays single and a repeating one (like a name's given names) becomes a list. If several answers are given for a single-valued element, the first is used and you get a warning. A repeating group whose item has a definition (for example a patient's contacts) produces one element per row the user filled in, and answers entered under another answer are included.

No resource id is made up: the extracted resources carry only what the form provided. Each Bundle entry gets a fresh urn:uuid address unless the extension says otherwise. The extension's own settings are honored — the profile to extract (added to the resource's meta.profile unless it is the plain resource type), the entry address (fullUrl) and the conditional-request settings (ifNoneMatch, ifMatch, ifNoneExist, ifModifiedSince), each given as a FHIRPath expression evaluated against the group's answers. Allocating ids across resources (extractAllocateId) and fixed values (definitionExtractValue) are not supported.

Supported resource types

The engine can build common resources — Patient, Condition, Observation, Encounter, Practitioner, Medication, MedicationRequest, Procedure, AllergyIntolerance and other types with straightforward element paths.

This is a basic implementation, not a full SDC definition-based extractor. Known limits:

  • The extension is only used as a marker: its own parameters (such as fullUrl or the conditional request options) are ignored, and the resource type is taken from each item's definition path.
  • Fields are filled from simple values; a coded answer is not converted to the shape of the target element, so check coded fields (for example Condition.code) in the result.
  • Answers nested under another answer are not read, and repeating groups that map to the same list element are merged into one entry.
  • Ids and fullUrl values in the bundle are generated placeholders, and the output is not validated against profiles.

These limits are tracked in the project issues; use an SDC server for extraction that needs full conformance.

Running it

  1. Fill in the form in the preview (or load a QuestionnaireResponse).
  2. Open Save ▾ → 🧩 Definition Extract · FHIR JSON Bundle.
  3. The builder produces a transaction Bundle containing one resource per annotated group, each populated from the mapped answers.

Everything runs in the browser — no server is required.

When to use it vs. Observation extraction

Use definition-based extraction when you need to populate specific fields of specific resource types (e.g. build a Patient and a Condition). Use Observation-based extraction when you simply want each coded answer to become an Observation. Both are described in Extraction.
